open_points.subject: canonical security-review grammar used to accept A21
open_points.text: The record follows the Workbench's canonical security-review grammar, a design fact of authoring that no generated code reads
open_points.question: Which exact grammar and revision determine the required category set and record validity, and does an accepted review remain governed by that revision after the Workbench grammar changes?
options: Pin the exact Workbench grammar revision and category set used when A21 is accepted.
Revalidate the record against the current Workbench grammar every time the State 2 gate runs.
Make the nine category names listed in this decision the authoritative closed set, independent of later Workbench grammar changes.
open_points.default_guess: Pin the exact Workbench grammar revision and category set used when A21 is accepted so an unchanged accepted design has reproducible gate results.

witness.initial: A21's displayed record has exactly the nine listed categories and passes the canonical Workbench grammar in effect when the review is accepted.
events: The Workbench maintainer publishes a new canonical grammar revision that adds one required category.
The owner changes none of States 0–2 or the A21 record.
An agent runs `design_lint --state 2` before proceeding to State 3.
outcomes: The record still passes because acceptance is evaluated using the grammar revision in effect at authoring time.
The record fails and State 3 is blocked because the gate uses the current grammar and the newly required category is missing.
witness.observer: The owner and the agent attempting to proceed to State 3
